Topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Decoding Information Theory

Target audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics)

Section: section_1 — The Hook: The Warden's Challenge

Lecture lines:
Warden places 64 coins on a chessboard grid.
One coin is flipped to hide the secret square.
Prisoner must identify the square to win freedom.

Planned animations:
Show a 2D grid of prisoners. Highlight one prisoner to represent the target. Color: #FFFFFF (grid), #FF0000 (target).
Animate the warden presenting a binary switch. Color: #00FF00 (switch).
Indicate the switch flipping state. Flash the switch to emphasize action. Color: #FFFF00 (flash).

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite: Binary Encoding

Lecture lines:
64 squares are represented by 6 binary bits.
Bit positions 0 through 63 define every square.
XOR parity acts as our digital checksum.

Planned animations:
Display binary numbers 0 and 1. Color: #00FFFF (0), #FF00FF (1).
Visualize bit sequence construction. Show bits shifting into a line. Color: #FFFFFF (bits).
Highlight the parity bit concept. Show it as an extra bit. Color: #FF0000 (parity bit).

Section: section_3 — The Information Strategy

Lecture lines:
Target square index is encoded into board parity.
Calculate XOR sum of all Heads positions.
Flip the one coin to match target index.
This ensures board parity equals target square.
Information is hidden within coin state distribution.

Planned animations:
Visualize groups of binary data chunks. Color: #FFFFFF (data).
Represent the strategy as a mapping function. Draw arrows between chunks. Color: #00FF00 (arrows).
Show successful data transmission using checkmarks. Color: #00FF00 (checkmarks).

Section: section_4 — Mathematical Proof via Parity

Lecture lines:
Flipping one coin changes exactly one parity bit.
This effectively corrects the total parity sum.
Parity acts as an error detection mechanism.
Mathematically map board state to unique square.
Proof confirmed: always identify the secret square.

Planned animations:
Show an input vector of bits. Color: #FFFFFF (input).
Perform the XOR operation visually. Show bit values interacting. Color: #FFFF00 (XOR operation).
Display the resulting parity bit output. Color: #00FF00 (output).

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: Information Theory Significance

Lecture lines:
Strategy applies Error Correction Code principles.
Information theory minimizes uncertainty via parity.
Technology uses this to fix data corruption.

Planned animations:
Show the connection between parity and error detection. Color: #FFFFFF (text).
Display an information theory formula. Highlight key parts. Color: #00FFFF (highlight).
Summarize the significance with a glowing conclusion text. Color: #FFFFFF (text).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Information Theory Significance", [
            "Strategy applies Error Correction Code principles.",
            "Information theory minimizes uncertainty via parity.",
            "Technology uses this to fix data corruption."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Parity bit concept visual
        parity_bit = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        parity_label = Text("Parity Bit", font_size=20)
        parity_group = VGroup(parity_bit, parity_label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(parity_group, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(parity_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Entropy/Uncertainty formula H = -sum(p log p)
        formula = MathTex(r"H = -\sum p_i \log p_i", color=TEAL)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TEAL))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Tech icon (simple rect representing data block)
        data_block = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2.0, color=GREEN)
        label = Text("Error-Corrected Data", font_size=18)
        data_group = VGroup(data_block, label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(data_group, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(data_group))
        self.play(data_group.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)
